## Natural history notes

A small case-bearing leaf beetle characterized by its compact cylindrical body, creamy yellow to dull orange wing covers, and two darker reddish to blackish lengthwise bands that may be faint or variable. In Florida, it has been recorded in open pine and prairie-associated habitats, including sites such as central Florida wildlife areas, and likely occurs on low vegetation, shrubs, or woodland-edge plants. Adults feed on plant material, while the larvae develop inside protective cases made from frass and debris, a typical trait of case-bearing leaf beetles.
